title: Prefill-aware cohort shaper with kernel-hinting for dynamic seqlen bucketing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce padding waste and tail-latency by forming prefill-aware request cohorts and exposing kernel-selection hints to the scheduler. The feature co-designs sequence-length bucketing, attention-optimized kernel hints, and prefill/decode scheduling to maintain latency SLOs while lowering per-token cost.
background: Current runtime bucketing is seqlen-only and schedules prefill and decode independently. Observed inefficiencies: (1) prefill requests with similar prefixes are not coalesced, causing duplicated KV materialization; (2) decode scheduling often interleaves short decodes with long prefill batches, increasing tail latency; (3) kernel selection lacks contextual hints about expected decode lengths and attention sparsity, leading to suboptimal kernel choices for some cohorts.
goals: 1) Reduce average padding tokens per-request by >=20% for mixed-length workloads. 2) Keep 95th-percentile latency within existing SLOs for all customer tiers. 3) Reduce duplicate KV materialization by coalescing prefill cohorts when safe. 4) Surface kernel hints to the runtime so kernel selection aligns with cohort characteristics.
success_metrics: - Padding reduction: percent decrease in pad tokens per million tokens processed (target 20%). - Cost impact: reduction in GPU token-seconds per API token (target 10%). - Latency: no regression on p95 and p99 compared to baseline. - KV duplication: percent requests benefiting from cached coalesced KV (target 30%).
constraints: - Must be runtime-safe: cannot change correctness of outputs. - Should work with model variants (quantized/float, sparse attention) and across dedicated/private deployments. - Changes must be reversible for canary/rollback. - Low overhead for coalescing decision logic (tight CPU budget on host).
proposal_summary: Introduce a prefill-aware cohort shaper: during request admission, annotate requests with origin prefix fingerprint and estimated decode length. Group admitted requests into short-lived cohorts that prioritize: kernel affinity (hint), prefix coalescing eligibility, and decode scheduling bucket. Scheduler uses these cohorts to pick prefill batching policy, select kernel backends appropriately, and sequence decode work to avoid tail-latency amplification.
design_decisions: - Fingerprint approach: use 64-bit rolling hash of normalized prefix (truncate to 64 bits) to detect coalescing candidates; risk: hash collisions but acceptable if a small fraction leads to no coalescing. - Kernel hints: expose attributes (expected_decode_len_bucket, attention_sparsity_hint, quantization_mode) in request metadata; runtime kernel selector uses hints as soft preferences. - Cohort lifetime: 20-100ms sliding window per device queue to balance batching gains vs latency. Tunable per deployment tier. - Fallbacks: if cohort coalescing fails or causes latency regressions, scheduler falls back to current seqlen-only bucketing.
implementation_steps: 1) Add prefix fingerprinting util in admission path and estimate_decode_len heuristic in request classifier.
2) Extend request proto with kernel_hint fields (enum + small int fields).
3) Implement cohort shaper module that creates ephemeral cohorts with attributes: target_seq_bucket, kernel_hint, coalesce_ok boolean.
4) Wire cohort shaper into the packer/prefill path; enable optional prefix coalescing where coalesce_ok is true.
5) Update kernel selector to accept soft hints and score kernels by expected throughput for cohort attributes.
6) Modify decode scheduler to prioritize finishing decodes for cohorts with tight latency budgets and avoid interleaving long prefill batches with short decodes.
7) Add feature flags and config knobs (cohort_window_ms, min_cohort_size, enable_kernel_hints) for canary/gradual rollout.
8) Add unit and integration tests, microbench harness, and end-to-end perf job.
9) Canary rollout on non-critical pool, gather metrics, iterate on thresholds and heuristics.
10) Full rollout with dashboarding and alert thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flagged internal-only experiments on dev cluster (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Canary on low-traffic region and dedicated pools (2 weeks), monitor padding and latency.
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 25% host traffic with autoscaling metrics tied to p95 latency (1 week).
Phase 3: Full rollout (post validation) with rollback gate if p95/p99 or error-rate exceeds thresholds.
Rollback: revert to seqlen-only packer by disabling cohort shaper flag.
testing_plan: Unit: hashing correctness, kernel_hint proto compatibility checks.
Integration: simulated mixed-length traffic replay using Replay Bench harness with synthetic prefixes to validate coalescing correctness.
Perf: A/B perf runs against representative workloads (chat, completion, embeddings heavy) measuring token-seconds and pad tokens.
Canary safety: maintain shadow-mode run that records but does not execute coalescing to detect behavioral drift.
Regression: automated p95/p99 smoke tests for each release.
monitoring_and_alerting: SLO alerts: p95/p99 latency increase >5% triggers PagerDuty to runtime-oncall.
Cost alerts: per-token GPU seconds deviation >10% triggers Ops review.
Data quality alerts: unexpected increase in KV duplication or failed coalesces.
Dashboard widgets: cohort vs seqlen pad comparison, kernel selection distribution by cohort.
